title: Redwood POC weekly sync - cost & perf review (BetaRetail)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on unit economics: tokens/sec/$, caching savings, and batching tradeoffs. Reviewed last week's benchmark, discussed tuning suggestions, and agreed next steps for the pilot.
action_items: Alex Chen; Send updated cost spreadsheet with tokens/sec/$ scenarios; 2025-04-15
Priya Nair; Run 2 more benchmark runs with cache enabled + 8k context; 2025-04-13
Jordan Lee; Share 1-week traffic trace (anonymized) for batching analysis; 2025-04-14
next_steps: Redwood to share updated cost model and benchmark artifacts
SE to run cache + batching sweeps and share results
Customer to review security docs and confirm pilot scope for Dedicated trial
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (BetaRetail SRE), Maya Patel (BetaRetail Product)

Summary: quick review of last week's POC benchmark focusing on tokens/sec per dollar, caching wins, and batching latency tradeoffs. Action items captured at end.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we got the core group, um, we'll keep this to about 40 minutes. quick agenda — results review, tuning notes, and next steps for the pilot.
[00:18] Jordan: sounds good, Alex. maya had to jump onto a customer call but she'll be here in a bit, I'm on for most of it.
[00:25] Priya: cool, I'll share the high-level numbers up front — ran the throughput sweep both with and without prefix/KV cache and with batching enabled at different sizes.
[00:38] Alex: perfect. just to remind, BetaRetail is running mixed workloads — short chat prompts for product search plus longer context summarization for returns workflows. we modeled both.
[00:50] Priya: right, so baseline hosted run (r1) no cache, small batch (batch=1): average tokens/sec about 320 tokens/sec on p4-equivalent, cost per 1M tokens came out to $18 using the hosted pricing assumptions. with cache enabled — prefix cache for repeated product descriptions — tokens/sec for effective requests rose to ~850 for cache hits because KV avoids recomputation, which translates to about $6.5 per 1M effective tokens when hit-rate is 60%.
[01:20] Maya: sorry I'm late — can you repeat the cache hit numbers?
[01:24] Priya: sure — with cache on and a ~60% hit rate we saw effective tokens/sec jump because many tokens are served from KV. raw model still emits tokens but the per-request compute is much lower for hits. think of it as per-effective-token cost dropping roughly 2.5x in our tests.
[01:40] Jordan: that 60% assumes product description reuse — is that realistic? our traces show about 40-50% reuse in peak, maybe 30% in some regions.
[01:50] Priya: yea so we ran sensitivity: at 40% hit rate cost advantage is ~1.8x; at 70% it's ~3x. we included the traces you sent last week for a smaller run and the model matched pretty closely.
[02:05] Alex: folks, one important bit — tokens/sec/$ is sensitive to sequence length. our bench used average seq len 120 for search and 800 for summarization workflows. long tails push effective tokens per second down.
[02:20] Maya: for returns summaries those 800s are a big driver of cost, yeah. can we do selective quantization there? you mentioned quantization profiles in the doc.
[02:28] Priya: correct, for summarization path we recommended INT8 quant for these checkpoints — that yields small quality delta but 20-30% faster token throughput on CPU-GPU hybrids. Redwood Optimize will propose per-model quant profiles; we can test those in the next run.
[02:45] Jordan: how does batching change that? we saw that with batch sizes 8-16 latency jumps for interactive search beyond your 300ms SLO.
[02:53] Priya: batching is the classic tradeoff — bigger batch improves tokens/sec and amortizes kernel costs, so tokens per dollar improves, but p99 latency degrades. for your interactive search path we propose adaptive batching: keep batch tiny (1-2) for low-latency routes and larger batch window (8) for background summarization.
[03:13] Alex: and we can route by policy in the Redwood runtime so the same model deployment serves both with per-route SLOs.
[03:21] Maya: okay, that helps. what about dedicated vs hosted cost modeling? our finance team asks if Dedicated reserved would be cheaper per token at our expected scale.
[03:30] Priya: great question — we ran a capacity model. at your committed throughput (avg 15k tokens/sec sustained) Dedicated with committed monthly GPUs gives about 25-35% lower unit cost after accounting for amortized infra and 24/7 utilization. but you need to hit utilization targets; otherwise burst and underutilization can make hosted more predictable.
[03:52] Jordan: what's the margin of error on that estimate? we have spiky traffic, Black Friday type spikes.
[03:57] Priya: we included burst policies in the model — Dedicated + burst to hosted will cover spikes, but bookkeeping: burst cost is higher, so effective blended unit cost depends on spike ratio. we recommended a 60% baseline utilization to justify Dedicated.
[04:12] Maya: can you show the numbers in a spreadsheet? the CFO wants an explicit tokens/sec/$ per scenario.
[04:18] Alex: we'll send the updated spreadsheet — that's one of the action items.
[04:22] Priya: another nuance — cache effectiveness can make Dedicated more attractive because a higher cache hit-rate reduces overall GPU time, so you may need fewer GPUs at same effective throughput.
[04:33] Jordan: hmm interesting. are there any consistency issues with cache across replicas? our infra folks worry about KV coherence.
[04:40] Priya: good call — Redwood's prefix/KV cache is per-shard with an eventual consistency model. for near real-time updates we can evict keys or have TTLs; we recommend short TTLs for inventory-adjacent keys. I'll put notes in the security/ops doc.
[04:56] Jordan: do you have benchmarks for 8k context windows? we want to test long summaries with 8k context.
[05:02] Priya: we ran an 8k context run (r3) — tokens/sec fell to ~140 on the baseline, but with cache on (where prefix cache captures repeated product info) effective tokens/sec recovered to ~420 for the hit portion. quality remained consistent. we'll run a larger sweep with your anonymized traces.
[05:21] Maya: what's the impact on cost for storing cache (memory) and KMS for encryption? security wants cost and compliance numbers.
[05:28] Alex: caching memory footprint adds modest infra cost; KMS per-request cost for envelope keys is minimal compared to GPU time, but we'll include those line items. also Redwood Private adds platform fees; we'll note that in the spreadsheet.
[05:41] Jordan: any competitors raised in your benchmarks? we tested OpenAI and Anthropic for short prompts last month.
[05:47] Priya: we included those as baselines; in many short prompt cases OpenAI had lower latency but higher cost per 1M tokens in our assumed pricing. Anthropic showed stronger safety for generative outputs in our eval, but unit cost varied. our cost model lets you plug in different price points.
[06:03] Maya: timeline — we want to decide on Dedicated pilot by end of next week. is that feasible?
[06:08] Alex: yes, provided we get the last traces and we run the two extra benchmark runs. Priya, you ok to prioritize?
[06:14] Priya: yep I'll prioritize the cache+batches sweep and the 8k runs, collate into the spreadsheet. expecting 48-72 hours for full runs.
[06:22] Jordan: I'll anonymize and drop the traffic trace into the shared folder today.
[06:26] Alex: great. any security blockers? Maya?
[06:29] Maya: from a compliance POV we need SOC2 scope items and SSO/SAML detail — we saw the summary doc but need the full artifact.
[06:36] Alex: we'll push the full security pack to the shared drive after this meeting — include SOC2 report, encryption details, RBAC, and audit log samples.
[06:44] Priya: quick note on performance tuning — you might get the best bang for buck by optimizing prompt templates: shorter prefixes and more structured system prompts reduce average sequence length and improve tokens/sec/$ significantly.
[06:56] Jordan: that's low hanging fruit; we'll coordinate with product to try tightening templates.
[07:00] Maya: ok let's recap next steps.
[07:03] Alex: recap: Redwood sends updated tokens/sec/$ spreadsheet with Dedicated vs Hosted scenarios, include cache memory/KMS/Private fees; SE runs cache & batching sweeps including 8k context and publishes results; BetaRetail provides anonymized traffic trace; Redwood shares full security artifacts. decision on Dedicated pilot target: 2025-04-18.
[07:23] Jordan: thanks, that works.
[07:25] Maya: thanks both.
[07:27] Alex: cool, we'll follow up via email and upload docs. end.

Notes on transcription: some words mis-heard (p4-equivalent sometimes transcribed as P4 EQ), speaker turns occasionally merged. timestamps approximate every ~20-40s.
